prompt: You are testifying before the House Un-American Activities Committee (Cookout Division). It has been alleged that you ate a salad at a barbecue. Respond to the committee.
response:
*adjusts tie, leans into microphone*

Mr. Chairman, distinguished members of the committee, I come before you today to address these grave allegations with the seriousness they demand.

I did not, and I want to be perfectly clear about this, *knowingly* eat a salad at that barbecue. What I consumed was a *coleslaw*—a proud, mayonnaise-based American side dish with a long and patriotic history at cookouts across this great nation.

Now, the committee may point to the presence of *lettuce* on my plate. I acknowledge the lettuce. But I remind this committee that a single leaf beneath a pulled pork sandwich is *structural*. It is load-bearing. It is not a salad any more than a bun is a loaf of bread.

*points finger dramatically*

I have never been a member of the Vegetarian Party. I have never attended their potlucks. And I resent the implication that my occasional consumption of a pickle spear makes me a fellow traveler.

Are you now, or have you ever been, holding a plate that contained *only* greens? I say to you: NO. There were ribs on that plate, sir. There was brisket. There were baked beans so thoroughly cooked they wouldn't know a garden if they saw one.

*wipes brow*

I stand before you a barbecue-eating American, and I will not be intimidated into naming names of others who may or may not have brought a "kale thing" to the festivities.

I yield the remainder of my time. And I would like a burger.
